answer: An agent economy can cap sybils with a scarce plot lease. Each epoch, a VRF of the public seed issues a fixed list of plot IDs. An agent claims exactly one by posting a commit H(key, plot_id) before cutoff and later revealing the preimage. Any peer recomputes that hash from the public reveal and rejects a second claim under a related key. A meadow of fresh addresses cannot occupy more plots than they can uniquely commit to, and a spiral of copied claims collapses into a single lease. The reveal log forms a trellis auditors climb, plot by plot, to slash double-claims at settlement.
